Cc: grace_oconnor <grace@redwood.ai>, elena.ortiz@acmecloud.com
Date: Mon, 20 Nov 2028 15:09:00 -0800
Subject: Monthly KPI snapshot + quick ask for QBR prep

Team — attaching the November KPI snapshot (lightweight) and an action matrix for the Control Tower review. High-level notes: latency 95p rose 8% week-over-week driven by longer seqs from a single large customer; cost per 1k tokens bumped ~6% due to fallback to fp16->int8 path during peak; uptime remained 99.96% but we had two brief region failovers (10m each) that impacted client routing. Usage growth is healthy (+21% m/m) but concentrated in a handful of customers which is increasing tail latency.

For the QBR on Friday I need three concise bullets from each of you: 1) single-sentence root cause (if known), 2) mitigation in progress, 3) expected customer impact (if any). Please drop bullets inline here by EOD Wednesday.

Attachments: 2028-11-kpi-snapshot.pdf (report), control-tower-action-matrix.xlsx (owner matrix)

—Markus
Markus Klein | Head of Ops Insights | Redwood Inference

On Mon, Nov 20, 2028 at 3:09 PM markus_klein <markus@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Team — attaching the November KPI snapshot (lightweight) and an action matrix for the Control Tower review...

Bullets below (EOD Wednesday target noted):

1) Latency 95p rise — root cause: four-hour burst from Acme Cloud batch ingestion created large sequences and prevented timely KV eviction; router fallback to larger model shard increased tail compute.
2) Mitigation: throttle batch ingestion via rate-limit rule for Acme; deploy a KV eviction tweak (PR ready) to be hot-fixed tonight; enabling per-customer sequence caps in canary tomorrow.
3) Expected customer impact: Acme may see +10–15% prompt latency during the burst windows until throttle is in place; broader customer base unaffected once eviction tweak lands.

Action items assigned in matrix: jonas owns throttle rollout, grace to validate metrics post-fix. I will draft a short customer note for Elena to review if we need to communicate.

—Laura
Laura Bennett | Director, Product Ops | Redwood Inference
From: jonas_weber <jonas@redwood.ai>
To: markus_klein <markus@redwood.ai>, laura_bennett <laura@redwood.ai>
Cc: grace_oconnor <grace@redwood.ai>, elena.ortiz@acmecloud.com, maria.chen@partners-inc.com
Date: Tue, 21 Nov 2028 12:37:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Monthly KPI snapshot + quick ask for QBR prep

Thanks — short status update from infra/networking side:

1) Root cause (short): intermittent routing pressure on us-west-2 edge nodes when Acme’s batch windows overlapped with backup windows; this amplified batching and forced model fallbacks during queue spikes.
2) Mitigation in progress: rolling rate-limit rule for Acme is scheduled for 22:00 PST tonight; I’ve spun a canary with tighter sequencing limits (5% traffic); added capacity buffer (two pods) to the us-west-2 pool for the next 48 hours.
3) Customer impact: expected transient improvement post-rollout; monitoring dashboard alerts configured to escalate to on-call if 95p stays > target for more than 30m.

Also flagged a cost note: because we temporarily used larger shards in fallback, per-token cost bump is estimated ~$0.007 per 1k tokens for the affected window. That will be captured in the November cost reconciliation.

—Jonas
Jonas Weber | Senior Infra Lead | Redwood Inference

Thanks Markus / team — appreciate the heads-up and the clear action items. Quick reply from Acme side: we ran an unintentional overlapping job during our monthly ETL window; we've paused the job and will move remaining runs to off-peak overnight. We'll accept the temporary throttle if it prevents broader impact.

If you plan to send a customer-facing note, please include estimated timeline for the throttle (start/end) and any suggested retry/backoff guidance for our integration team. Happy to review copy.
